national.title: Feds charge powerful Virginia Democrat in alleged drug scheme
national.summary: L. Louise Lucas, a longtime state senator from Virginia, has been arrested in connection with an alleged bribery and racketeering scheme.
national.body: Norfolk, Virginia — L. Louise Lucas, a powerful Virginia state senator and vocal Trump critic who played a central role in the state's redistricting effort last year, was taken into federal custody Thursday and charged in connection with an alleged bribery and racketeering scheme, the Justice Department said.According to a 45-page indictment filed in the Eastern District of Virginia, Lucas and six other co-defendants are charged with conspiring to distribute and possess marijuana, conspiring to launder money, laundering money and committing bribery by distributing large quantities of illegal marijuana under the auspices of her legal medical cannabis business.A federal grand jury returned the indictment last week. Lucas, 82, surrendered to law enforcement on Thursday morning. She faces five of the eight charges included in the indictment. Lucas is set to make her initial appearance before a federal magistrate judge Thursday afternoon. He said there was "nothing improper" about the timing of the indictment.The case comes nearly six months after federal law enforcement searched Lucas' office and a shop called The Cannabis Outlet that she co-owns in Portsmouth, Virginia. One source familiar with the investigation told CBS News at the time of the search that the investigation started during the Biden administration. national.title: Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield, and what they mean to Ukraine
national.summary: Here's what to know about Starlink and Starshield, the technologies Ukraine is relying on in the war against Russia.
national.body: Over the past week, Ukraine has received a stark reminder of its growing dependence on uninterrupted access to Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield networks in its drone-heavy war against Russia, now in its fifth year.Ukraine has a fraction of Russia's resources, but its aggressive development of drone warfare on defensive and offensive fronts has helped it endure an onslaught from its much bigger adversary, which invaded Ukraine in early 2022. That was true until last week, when Ukraine reported a throttling of the Starshield network that was causing its drones to stop midflight and fall out of the sky.The two SpaceX networks operate on a constellation of thousands of low-Earth satellites — Starlink is the commercial version, while Starshield is a military product licensed to the U.S. government and its partners, among them Ukraine.Kyiv's reliance on drones has made Starlink and Starshield nearly indispensable to its arsenal. When Ukraine experienced a disruption to those networks, it lost the shield of interceptors and drones that offered some protection against Russian drone and missile strikes.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy believes Musk throttled Starshield at the request of U.S. officials, though the world's richest man has denied any role and said it's the U.S. government that controls the military-grade network. President Trump has also denied he's responsible for slowing the network. However, CBS News reported Tuesday that Musk was behind the disruption, which occurred after he spoke with administration officials multiple times seeking clarity on the president's thinking on the matter, according to sources familiar with the situation.There has also been conflicting information about whether full access to the networks has been restored. As of Wednesday afternoon, Starlink remained throttled, Zelenskyy's office confirmed. national.title: Toledo man describes days-long chemical leak: "Looked like a movie"
national.summary: Hundreds of people remain evacuated from their homes days after the chemical leak began at a facility in Toledo, Ohio.
national.body: Hundreds of people in Toledo, Ohio, remain evacuated from their homes as officials work to resolve a fiery chemical leak that began Tuesday.Residents within a mile of an MC Tank facility were order to evacuate on Tuesday, and everyone within a 3-mile radius was told to shelter in place. On Wednesday, the shelter-in-place was lifted and evacuations were reduced to half a mile. They were reduced further, to a quarter-mile, by Thursday morning. But a chemical plume remains. City officials have been allowing the chemicals to vent from the 5,500-gallon tank, instead of trying to send in crews to stop the leak. Toledo Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz said Wednesday that the potential for an explosion made it too dangerous for first responders, including hazardous material teams, to approach the tank. One first responder has sustained injuries, Kapszukiewicz said.The city and MC Tank Transport Inc. said the substance involved in the leak is glycidyl methacrylate, an industrial chemical that is used in plastics, paints and coatings. State officials said the leak happened due to an error as the chemical was being transferred. Residents have reported symptoms including burning in the eyes, lungs and sinuses, bad headaches and nausea. One area hospital is treating 35 patients. Resident Travis Williams said he "woke up choking" from overwhelming fumes."I've never had these feelings, the burnings, itchy skin, irritated eyes," Williams said. "I am definitely worried about the long-term effect of this." A dense fog has also descended over Toledo. Officials say the fog was indistinguishable from the chemical plume. The conditions are also affecting visibility. Williams said the scene outside his home "looked like a movie." "I couldn't even see as far as my car to the curb," Williams said. Officials are asking residents to ventilate their homes by opening windows and doors. Residents are also being encouraged to wash their hands thoroughly and watch for coughing and eye irritation in people and pets. The Environmental Protection Agency is monitoring air quality. In May, an industrial tank containing another methacrylate compound ruptured in Orange County, California. That incident displaced thousands until a crack formed in the overheating tank, relieving the pressure and ending the risk of explosion.

national.title: WWII fighter plane wreckage, pilot's personal items found in Hungary
national.summary: The remains of a downed Soviet fighter plane from World War II were uncovered recently in a remote Hungarian town, officials said.
national.body: The wreckage of a World War II-era Soviet jet was discovered in rural Hungary, along with some of its pilot's personal items, according to the Hungarian Museum of Military History and local media.Excavators unearthed the Soviet Yakovlev Yak-1 fighter aircraft from about 17 feet underground in the central Hungarian village of Törtel, which is located about 50 miles southeast of Budapest, museum officials said. István Kocsis, a member of the research association who led the investigation into the wreck, said excavations in the area began in September.Several portions of the plane were relatively intact when archaeologists recovered them from the crash site. The relics included what officials identified as a piece of the red star insignia printed on all Soviet military properties at the time, which they said was "in relatively good condition." Part of the aircraft's fuselage was also recovered, displaying the jet's side number, in addition to the pilot's personal belongings. Among them was a book containing the pilot's signature, which experts at the museum are currently working to restore, the museum said.Some of the best-preserved pieces of the wreck will be exhibited by the military museum, once its archaeology department has finished carrying out restoration procedures and logged records of their obervations.Although scientists and archaeologists alike are still working to learn more about the decades-old debris, they were able to trace the wreckage back to a particular wartime crash that took place in November 1944, Hungarian local media reported. While opposing each other over Törtel, German Lt. Peter Düttmann and Soviet Lt. Alexander Semyonovich Andrianov's aerial duel ended with Düttmann shooting down the Soviet aircraft. Although Andrianov escaped by parachute, he later became a prisoner of war, according to the news site Hungary Today.

national.title: Childcare costs are growing faster than rent in the U.S.
national.summary: A growing share of American families are having to shell out more than $2,000 a month for childcare services, new data shows.
national.body: The rising cost of childcare in the U.S. is vying with food prices and healthcare expenses in straining household budgets.Nearly 8% of families are spending more than $2,000 per month on childcare services, including daycare, nanny services and other programs. That's more than double the share of households that spent that much just three years ago, according to new research from the Bank of America Institute. In September, the cost of daycare and school-related fees rose faster than other essential expenses, such as rent and medical care, compared to the same period a year ago, according to federal labor data. Families nationwide spent an average of 8% of their monthly incomes on childcare services in September, BofA found. Under federal guidelines, childcare is considered affordable when it consumes no more than 7% of household income. Assuming a family spends $24,000 annually on childcare, it would need to earn roughly $343,000 to remain below the 7% threshold. In 2025, median household income was $87,460, according to Census Bureau data. Lower- and middle-income families spend nearly 9% of their annual incomes on childcare payments, while higher-income households spend 7.3%, according to BofA. Along with facing rising childcare costs, workers have also seen slowing wage growth, heightening the financial pressure on many families, Economic Policy Institute economist Elise Gould told CBS News.Separate research from AARP shows that families are turning to grandparents, who provide $172 billion per year in direct financial assistance. Where are childcare costs growing fastest? In some parts of the U.S., childcare fees are rising even faster, according to BofA. In September, median childcare costs rose fastest in Nashville, Tennessee, followed by Jacksonville, Florida, and Phoenix, Arizona, compared to the same period a year ago, according to BofA's analysis."There's been an increase in domestic migration to these areas," BofA Institute economist Taylor Bowley told CBS News, noting that an increase in demand for childcare services is putting pressure on prices. A shortage of childcare workers also appears to be driving up childcare expenses. In the new campaign, a mock-prison cell is suspended several stories high over Tajrish Square, in an upscale neighborhood of north Tehran. national.summary: A veteran North Korea analyst tells CBS News "a change in the situation" along the DMZ, and a warning from the North, are cause for concern.

She also warned Seoul of "the most horrible and distressing situation" if South Korea continues what Pyongyang called interference in North Korean internal affairs. "This is not a threat," she said, "but a clear warning."On Wednesday, Kim Yo Jung joined senior military officials to visit fortification sites along the border, where she said North Korean tactical units had taken up positions. She accused South Korean forces of broadcasting warning messages and firing warning shots at multiple locations near the border. South Korea acknowledged that its forces had fired warning shots, calling them "legitimate and defensive measures."North Korea expert Bob Carlin, a former U.S. State Department analyst who took part in negotiations with Pyongyang and has followed the country closely for four decades, told CBS News that Kim's statements about "tactical units" are a cause for concern."Whether these have heavy weaponry or not, this represents a change in the situation along the front," said Carlin. "Kim Yo Jung also spoke of the possibility of 'deploying more tactical strike means.' This sounds more like artillery and battlefield missile units, and if the decision has been made to move these up, it will be an even more serious change along the front lines."Is China worried that North Korea wants "to confront the U.S."? national.title: iPhone Duo already backordered until 2027 as pre-order sales soar
national.summary: Consumer demand for Apple's first foldable phone is strong despite the device's hefty $1,999 price tag.
national.body: Apple is seeing strong demand for its new foldable iPhone, with supplies quickly selling out after pre-order sales opened on Friday."Apple opened iPhone Duo pre-orders this morning, and the early read looks robust in our view, with demand for Cupertino's first foldable running well ahead of supply out of the gates," Wall Street analyst Dan Ives, a partner at Yorkville Ives, said in a research note.The pre-order window for the Duo opened on Friday at 8 a.m. ET on apple.com and in the Apple Store app. Within minutes, the estimated delivery of the phone was pushed back past Oct. 23, the device's official launch date, and into next year. As of Friday afternoon, the Apple phone was backordered until late January."It's been 3 minutes, and it's sold out at every store around the NYC/CT area," Max Weinbach, an analyst for the market research firm Creativestrat, said on X.Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment on how many pre-order requests it received. When the Duo officially launches on Oct. 23, Apple said it will have some inventory at its stores, but noted that supply could sell out quickly."On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," an Apple spokesperson said in an email. "Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we're working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible."Apple's new CEO, John Ternus, announced the iPhone Duo last month. The Duo lets users split the screen to use two different apps on the device, or two windows of the same website for uses such as comparison shopping.Prices start at $1,999 for a device with 256 GB of storage. When folded, it's about the size of a passport. The full display is the largest of any Apple phone, resembling more of an iPad than an iPhone.Ternus also announced the iPhone 18 at Apple's annual fall showcase, which went on sale last month.Ives thinks demand for the Duo will remain strong into 2027, with many iPhone users planning to upgrade. He projects Apple will sell around 10 million Duos in the next few quarters and up to 25 million in 2027.

national.title: Why a student protest movement is challenging 12 years of Vučić rule in Serbia
national.summary: After two years of student protests, Serbians vote on Sunday in elections that could bring down the ruling party.
national.body:
Rallies have been taking place across Serbia on Thursday, the final day of campaigning ahead of a snap election billed as a referendum on the country's future.

After two years of student protests, Serbians vote for a new parliament on Sunday in elections that threaten populist leader Aleksandar Vučić's 12 years in power.

The main threat to Vučić's dominance in Serbian politics comes from a two-year-old student movement, but there are concerns surrounding the fairness of the vote.

They have no obvious leaders and are not used to politics, but the "Student List-Students Win" movement has attracted anti-government voters across Serbia.

The Student List is fielding candidates from across Serbian society - and as he joined students marching towards Belgrade, lead candidate and cardiologist Ilija Srdanović said history was being rewritten: "The energy is unstoppable."

It all began on 1 November 2024, when the concrete canopy collapsed outside Novi Sad train station, in Serbia's second biggest city, killing 16 people.

The tragedy was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence in Serbia. Critics linked the station's fatally flawed renovation to a president who had closely associated himself with the project.

What started as weekly student protests demanding justice on university campuses and city streets soon became a national movement, often at a local level, that encompassed far more sections of Serbian society, including farmers, actors and judges.

national.body: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg threatened to move out of California if residents of the state approve a first-of-its-kind billionaire wealth tax when voters head to the polls on Nov. 3, the company said in a new regulatory filing. Because of his concerns over the wealth tax, Zuckerberg told Meta that he was "evaluating relocating his primary residence outside California and that steps toward any such relocation, including any listing of his residential real estate in California on the market, would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees and, accordingly, raise questions for management of the company going forward," the filing states.Meta said that because Zuckerberg's presence near the company's Menlo Park, California, headquarters is "critically important" to its success, the company took an unusual step: Its board approved a new class of nonvoting common stock that he can sell to raise cash to pay the wealth tax, if voters approve it. Without that change, Zuckerberg faced the prospect of having to sell voting shares to raise funds to pay the tax, which would have reduced his control of Meta. As a result of that decision to issue new stock, Zuckerberg has told Meta he will commit to remaining a California resident for eight years. If Meta moves its headquarters to another state, Zuckerberg will move to that jurisdiction, according to the regulatory filing. The disclosure highlights the public debate over the proposed billionaire wealth tax, known as Proposition 40, which will be on the Nov. 3 ballot in California. Under the proposal, the tax would impose a one-time 5% state tax on billionaire wealth — about $12.4 billion of Zuckerberg's estimated $247 billion net worth, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.The company believes "it is critically important to keep Mr. Zuckerberg in a leadership position with our company and that he continue to reside in and manage the company from our headquarters in California to ensure his continued ability to effectively drive our performance during this era of unprecedented challenge and competition in our industry," Meta said in its filing. national.title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda in patient who later died
national.summary: A first known human case of Shamonda virus infection has been detected in France, the country's health authorities said on Thursday.
national.body:
PARIS (AP) — A first known human case of Shamonda virus infection has been detected in France, the country's health authorities said on Thursday.

The virus was detected in a severely immunocompromised patient who was being treated for a serious illness in Lyon and died in early October.

France's health ministry said that based on current knowledge of the virus, no public health risk to the general population has been identified to date. Until now, the Shamonda virus was considered incapable of infecting humans.

"This is therefore an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient," according to the ministry.

Shamonda virus is transmitted to animals by biting midges. First detected in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, it has been reported sporadically in cattle in West, East and Southern Africa, as well as in Japan. It was identified for the first time in Europe this summer on cattle farms.

The patient was likely infected through a midge bite in eastern France, where the virus was reported to be circulating among animals during spring and summer, the ministry said.

French health authorities have notified international health bodies, including the World Health Organization and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.

national.title: Teacher who survived Oregon school shooting recounts playing dead
national.summary: Becky Drury, the 54-year-old teacher wounded in the shooting at an Oregon elementary school last week, says she was shot before she had "any chance to act."
national.body: Becky Drury, the 54-year-old teacher wounded in the shooting at an Oregon elementary school last week, is sharing a statement about her experience, saying the gunman shot her before she had "any chance to act."In the statement Wednesday, Drury recalled running to see what was happening outside her classroom at Silver Rail Elementary School before spotting the shooter."I turned to shut the door behind me, but the shooter was already there," Drury wrote. "Before I could do anything more, he shot me at close range and I fell to the ground.""Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured," she continued. "I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else. So, I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again."Drury suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries from the Oct. 15 shooting that killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a 25-year-old teacher. Another student, a 7-year-old, was also seriously wounded.The suspect was identified as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, a former student at the school. Police said he shot through the school's locked doors before entering a special needs classroom and opening fire.The gunman was tackled by another teacher and fatally shot by an armed bystander, 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco, who followed him into the school, according to police. Drury said Wednesday she was sharing what happened to her because "I want to make sure the events of that day and my actions in particular are reported accurately.""I know there has been contradictory reporting about my actions that day, but the truth is I was shot before I had any chance to act," she wrote.She thanked those who have supported her since the shooting, and said, "What happened in that classroom was unimaginable, and like so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy."

national.title: U.K. interests in the Arctic are vulnerable to Russia, lawmakers warn
national.summary: A group of British lawmakers called on the government to "urgently address" what it says are gaps in maritime forces in the Arctic.
national.body: "Glaring gaps" in the United Kingdom's Arctic defenses are leaving it and NATO vulnerable to attacks from Russia, British lawmakers said in a parliamentary report published Thursday.The group urged the British government to "urgently address" gaps in maritime forces, particularly with the U.S. acting "more unilaterally in the region." "This is a demanding, hostile environment, and one that our greatest adversary, Russia, is seeking to dominate for military advantage," Tan Dhesi, Chair of the Commons Defense Committee, wrote. The committee said that a "shockingly low availability" of Royal Navy submarines and warships means critical infrastructure, such as underwater cables and energy supplies, are exposed to potential Russian attacks. "Russia can then use the ice to conceal and protect its own submarines while threatening NATO sea lanes, U.K. critical infrastructure and the U.K.'s nuclear deterrent," the report added.The report urged Canada and European NATO allies to "take more responsibility for defence of their interests in the High North." Like European NATO countries, the United Kingdom lacks "some critical military capabilities that it has largely relied on the U.S. to provide, such as ballistic missile defence, long range strike and intelligence and surveillance assets, which will take considerable investment and time to replicate." "If the U.K. is to lead an effective coalition," the report continued, "it must address glaring gaps in the availability of its current maritime forces and ensure it has an agreed plan, integrated with European allies in the region, to deter and, if necessary, defeat any aggression in the High North from 2030."'To deter war we must be ready for it'Former British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer warned in June that Russia could attack NATO countries by the end of the decade.Conservative shadow minister for war readiness Stuart Anderson said that if Starmer's predictions are accurate, "time is just as important as money." "To deter war we must be ready for it, that means spending money now, not kicking the can down the road until it's too late," Anderson said.

national.title: Stephen Hubbard back in U.S. after release from Russian prison
national.summary: Hubbard, a Michigan native, spent four years wrongfully imprisoned in Russia before being released on Wednesday.
national.body: Stephen Hubbard, the Michigan native who spent four years wrongfully imprisoned in Russia before being released on Wednesday, landed back in the U.S. late Wednesday, according to President Trump.The president said Hubbard had just landed back in the U.S. while Mr. Trump spoke to reporters late Wednesday night as he returned from a rally in South Carolina. He expected Hubbard to visit the White House "in the next day or so.""He's obviously just got out of prison," Mr. Trump told reporters. "He was there for a long time."Hubbard's release was announced earlier in the day during a meeting between U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Hubbard was imprisoned in Russia for more than four years after being accused of fighting for Ukraine. The U.S. government had deemed Hubbard wrongfully detained.In a brief phone call with his father before Hubbard took off from St. Petersburg, his son, friar Joseph Coleman, said he sounded better than he had during their last conversation in May 2025."I want to embrace him as a son embraces his father. I want to personally assess his health to make sure he's well," Coleman said.Hubbard, 74, landed in San Antonio, where he will receive a medical evaluation, as is typical for prisoners released from overseas.Hubbard, a retired schoolteacher, was captured in Ukraine shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022 and was accused of manning a checkpoint for mercenaries. He was later sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony. His family has always disputed the charges.Mr. Trump said in social media posts that Putin agreed to release Hubbard at his request, with "no 'swap' necessary," though he also said he would not have been released had the White House not halted new sanctions passed by Congress against Russia from taking effect last week."It would seem that this is all tethered to short-term interests on the part of the Trump administration that seem to be connected to fuel prices," CBS News national security analyst Elliot Ackerman, a retired Marine and special activities officer at the CIA, told "CBS Mornings."Witkoff praised Putin after the release, calling him a "humanitarian," a comment that generated bipartisan criticism."You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian, you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that," Witkoff told Putin. national.title: Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
national.summary: The teacher said she could not help children because she was badly injured by the attacker.
national.body:
A 54-year-old teacher who survived a mass shooting at an Oregon elementary school said she pretended to be dead so the gunman would not shoot her again.

Becky Drury, a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School, said in a statement shared with US media that as she tried to shut her classroom door, the gunman shot her and she fell to the floor.

"I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again," Drury said.

The attacker - who has been identified as a 16-year-old former student at the school - killed three students and a teacher before a parent from the school fatally shot him.

In her first remarks since the 15 October shooting in Bend, Oregon, Drury said that she went to see what was happening outside the special-education classroom, and after spotting the shooter, she tried to shut the door.

The attacker still managed to shoot her, so she could not help any of the children in the classroom.

"Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured," she said. "I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else."

Drury suffered serious but not life-threatening harm from the shooting, which killed five-year-old Rhoam Summer, an eight and eleven-year-old, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert.

national.title: YouTuber arrested after popular Indian finance influencer's suicide
national.summary: V Harish, who ran the hugely popular Instagram account "Finance with Harish", was found dead on Tuesday.
national.body:
A 27-year-old finance influencer's suicide in India has been mired in allegations of cyberbullying and started a conversation around who should give financial advice to investors.

V Harish - who ran a hugely popular Instagram account called "Finance with Harish" - was found dead on Tuesday morning at his home near Chennai, capital of the southern state of Tamil Nadu.

His suicide came just weeks after his account was disabled by Meta after complaints of irregularities.

In a complaint lodged with the police, his father J Vinayagam has alleged that his son took his life because of online harassment by Jason Samuel, a YouTuber and CEO of tech-centric venture studio Zemuria.

Police arrested Samuel on Thursday under suspicion of trying to "extort money from Harish" and posting "defamatory videos against him on social media".

BBC Tamil has not been able to reach him for comment. Earlier, he denier wrongdoing in a post on X.

The case has brought into focus the growing influence of financial content creators in India, where millions of first-time investors increasingly turn to social media for market advice.

Harish began posting videos about finance and investing around five years ago, building a substantial online following.

national.title: Should you use home equity to pay off credit card debt? Here's when it can backfire.
national.summary: Your home's equity could offer a way out of expensive debt, but the potential savings come with serious trade-offs.

If you carry a balance when rates are elevated, a substantial portion of your credit card payment goes toward interest charges rather than the debt itself. national.body:
Hannah Fingerhut, Associated Press Hannah Fingerhut, Associated Press

DES MOINES, Iowa (AP) — After Ashley Hinson dropped off her boys at school earlier this month, she saw the initials "DJT" flash on her phone.

President Donald Trump is expected to speak at a rally in Sioux City, Iowa, at 6:30 p.m. EDT. Watch live in our video player above.

"'Ashley, it's your favorite president,'" Iowa's Republican nominee for U.S. Senate recently recounted to an audience of her supporters. "That's how he introduced himself."

She had had a more forceful message about communicating with President Donald Trump on the debate stage with her Democratic opponent, Josh Turek, as she tried to win over undecided voters.

"I'll be President Trump's ally when it is important for Iowa, but I will push back on him," promised Hinson, who currently serves in the U.S. House. "He knows this."

Although many Republicans are walking a political tightrope in this year's midterm elections, Hinson's balancing act is more challenging than most. Iowans have been hamstrung by manufacturing job losses, health care clinic closures and shrunken farm profits since Trump returned to the White House, but Hinson also is relying on the president's loyalists to show up for her.

On Thursday, Hinson will join Trump for a rally in Sioux City, which is in Iowa's conservative northwest corner. The visit to safe territory is geared toward boosting turnout even as it ties her more tightly to an unpopular president.

national.title: In final Michigan Senate debate, El-Sayed and Rogers question each other's loyalties
national.summary: This time, the exchanges focused on policy, though both candidates repeatedly returned to their central attacks.
national.body:
Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers clashed in their final Senate debate Wednesday, with El-Sayed trying to tie his opponent to President Donald Trump and Rogers saying his rival's progressive policies would be too extreme for Michigan.

The debate kicked off a breakneck final stretch in one of the nation's most closely watched and competitive Senate races. Former President Barack Obama will rally in Detroit on Saturday, followed by Trump on Sunday.

Wednesday's hourlong debate followed one on Oct. 8 that devolved into personal insults and attacks, with the candidates continuing to argue even during a commercial break. This time, the exchanges were slightly less contentious and focused on policy, though both candidates repeatedly returned to their central attacks.

"Those playing MAGA bingo at home, you just heard like three of the buzzwords," El-Sayed said after Rogers criticized his policies. Rogers later shot back: "The bingo game ought to be how many times can he put the word Trump in any answer."

The most contentious exchange came when Rogers again tried to link El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, repeating an allegation he and Trump have raised in recent weeks. El-Sayed has denied any affiliation with the group.

"If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America, or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers said.

El-Sayed, who would be the country's first Muslim senator, called Rogers' questioning of his commitment to the Constitution "shameful."

national.title: First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say
national.summary: The disease, which usually affects cattle, has been identified in a patient who died in early October.
national.body:
The first known human case of the Shamonda virus (Shav) has been detected in a patient who died in early October, French authorities have said.

Health officials said it was an "exceptional case in a severely immunocompromised patient" and there was currently no risk to the public.

Shav is a disease that primarily affects cattle and can be spread by infected midges. Cases have also occurred in sheep, goats, alpacas and horses, but infections in people were previously unheard of.

The World Health Organization (WHO) and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) said they were monitoring the situation, with French officials still investigating how the virus had spread to a human.

It is currently thought the patient contracted Shav through a midge bite in eastern France, the country's health and agriculture ministries said on Thursday, where cases were first identified in animals in the spring.

They said the patient was being treated for a serious illness in a Lyon hospital and experienced neurological complications thought to have been "very likely linked" to the virus, based on initial findings.

The statement stressed that their immune system was weakened, leaving them more vulnerable to getting ill.

"Until now, the Shamonda virus was considered non-transmissible to humans," it noted, having only been identified in animals "despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia".

national.title: Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
national.summary: The Iguazú Falls span more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October, which scientists link to the Super El Niño, has sent near-record volumes of water surging over the towering cliffs.
national.body:
Carrie Kahn/NPR IGUAZÚ NATIONAL PARK, Argentina — Few times in my life have I felt the enormity and power of nature. Standing at the edge of Iguazú Falls, on the Brazil-Argentina border, was one of them.

Iguazú isn't just one imposing fall, but a complex of cascades spanning more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October in Brazil has sent near-record volumes of water surging over its towering cliffs. Scientists link the relentless rains to this year's Super El Niño , causing extreme weather events across the globe.

But what a spectacular force of nature for the lower-than-average number of tourists who braved the deluge this month. The roar of the rushing Iguazú river under your feet penetrates your body; your eyes strain to keep up as the rusty swells disappear over the steep precipice. One day during my recent visit, officials registered nearly 12 million liters (more than 3 million gallons) of water per second tumbling over the falls. That's 10 times the normal flow. As the Iguazú river's red, muddy waters raced furiously toward the falls' edge, they lapped the bottom of the narrow metal catwalks that usually hover a few feet above the falls during normal-rainfall years. Officials closed the spectacular walkways as the river level kept rising. When asked why access was shut off, the national park's director simply said, "It just keeps raining." That's an understatement. I'm still drying out.

national.body: Americans are facing a "food insecurity crisis" after shouldering an additional $22 billion in food costs due to rising inflation and billions of dollars in food-stamp cuts, according to Sen. Elizabeth Warren. In an Oct. 21 letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, the Massachusetts Democrat said that the combination of rising food prices and cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program has created a "one-two punch" for millions of households. Warren also asked the USDA to work with lawmakers to reverse food-stamp policies that have resulted in 5.2 million people losing SNAP benefits since July 2025.SNAP enrollment, now at its lowest level since 2019, could shrink in the coming months as additional changes to the program take effect, according to anti-hunger experts. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), a tax and spending law signed into law by President Trump in 2025, expanded SNAP's work requirements and shifted more of the program's costs onto states. Those changes have created new hurdles for enrollment, according to experts.The USDA halted its annual study on food insecurity in 2025, saying at the time that the report was "redundant, costly [and] politicized." But a May analysis from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found "a remarkable increase in food insecurity, particularly among lower-educated and lower-income households and households with young children."The New York Fed found earlier this year that 10% of U.S. families reported they didn't have enough food and that their children sometimes missed meals, more than double the 4% share in 2020. national.body:
Yemen's Houthi movement has said it carried out an attack on an airport in eastern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday evening, which Saudi authorities said killed two people and injured eight others.

The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation identified those killed at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam as a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident.

It did not say what type of attack occurred, but the Iran-backed Houthis said on Thursday that the airport was one of the sites they had targeted with drones and missiles over the previous 48 hours.

Two more people were killed on Wednesday morning by debris from a drone that was intercepted elsewhere in Eastern Province, the Saudi energy ministry said.

The drone was intercepted as it attempted to target a processing facility owned by Saudi Arabia's state oil company Aramco in the Shaybah oil field, where a contractor's vehicle was set ablaze, according to the ministry.

It identified the dead as residents from the Philippines and Nepal.

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, did not claim the attack on the oil field.

In addition to Dammam's airport, he said they had targeted the Saudi defence ministry's headquarters building in the capital, Riyadh, an Aramco facility in the Red Sea city of Yanbu, and Abha International Airport in the south of the country.

national.title: Ilhan Omar says 'bizarre' pre-dawn raid on her home is forcing her to move out
national.summary: The congresswoman said federal agents seized over a dozen items, including cell phones and notebooks, as part of a federal investigation.
national.body:
Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar has said she can no longer live in her Washington DC home after it was searched by federal agents last week, fearing her address has been exposed after the raid.

"With the death threats that I deal with, it's not, it's no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids," she told MSN NOW , external .

In Omar's first public interview since the pre-dawn search of her home, she detailed how Homeland Security Investigations agents seized over a dozen items, including cell phones and notebooks, as part of an investigation.

The government has not said what crime Omar is accused of but that the raid was "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation".

The search follows multiple comments from officials that cast doubt on Omar's US citizenship, which she received in 2000 after her arrival from Kenya.

More than a dozen subpoenas have also been issued to members of Omar's family, as part of the investigation, and it was reported that her personal computers and passport were among the items that were seized.

Recalling the hourslong raid of her home with MS NOW, Omar said: "It obviously did freak all of us out."

Omar said agents began "pounding on the doors" of her home at around 06:00 EDT (11:00 BST) on 12 October, startling her and her husband, who were both in bed.

national.summary: The Swiss government told the BBC that the freed national was on her way back to Switzerland.
national.body:
Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi.

Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year.

No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed.

The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens.

The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts".

"We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... For many months, we worked closely, discreetly, and in a spirit of trust with our regional, European, and international partners. These joint efforts have paid off," Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger said in a statement.

national.title: AI discovered a software vulnerability that could impact 70% of websites worldwide. The rush is on to patch it
national.summary: Governments and corporations worked throughout the night to update software.
national.body:
Governments and corporations worked throughout the night to update software after the AI-assisted discovery of vulnerabilities in a programming language vital to about 70% of websites globally.

Many government sites appeared to be working Thursday, but outages or limited service remained while security work was under way.

The FBI's cyber division warned on Wednesday that the vulnerabilities could allow malicious actors to remotely execute code in the programming language, PHP, which powers websites and web applications. That raised the risk of sensitive data and networks being compromised, said the agency, which recommended that operators take websites offline if they can't update them immediately.

In Britain some "limited" government services may temporarily be offline while work is carried out to address potential cybersecurity issues, the prime minister's office said.

"Work has already taken place across Government to identify and fix potential exposures to our systems, and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue," a spokeswoman said Thursday.

"No large public-facing critical services are being affected by the exercise, but some limited services may temporarily be offline while security work is carried out, the spokeswoman said.

The government of Finland's website said that the disruption had been resolved, but that "some content is still missing and is currently being restored."

The Japanese Prime Minister shared a warning from the government in a social media post, advising website administrators to check if they use PHP and to immediately install a patch that was released late Wednesday.

national.title: How Maine voters feel about the high-stakes Senate election
national.summary: The state is both fired up by this big race and exhausted by its avalanche of ads.
national.body:
A state of no-nonsense, neighborly people, Maine is a unique place — full of practicality, hardiness and internal warmth.

Two days ago, I sat looking at an incredible scene from its exact geographic center : A blaze of fall leaves over the Pleasant River in Brownville Junction. Our small crew spent days crisscrossing and covering the U.S. Senate race. It is one of the most grueling campaigns for both candidates and voters of any I can remember.

I can honestly tell you, I don't know which way this race goes. But in that calm moment by the river, I started envisioning this guide about this high-stakes race.

Republican Sen. Susan Collins reaches out to shake hands with Brownville Fire Chief Shawn Mitchell. Photo by Lisa Desjardins/PBS News

Our time with Sen. Susan Collins was unusual because of what it was not.

At the Brownville Fire Department's annual dinner, we watched as the Republican senator entered, smiling and at ease.

In the middle of a high-stakes, intense campaign, this was remarkably not a campaign event. It was a small community gathering of a few dozen. The fire chief politely asked us not to record any of it except the senator's remarks.

For an hour or so, Collins sat to the side and in the back, saying hello to those near her but not intruding into the crowd. If she was anxious, it did not show.

At least four people have died in France, and one other has been injured, after flooding caused by Storm Adam.

The storm triggered widespread flooding across southern France on Tuesday, inundating streets and disrupting transport.

The deaths included two women aged 86 and 26 who were found drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-Rhône region.

Corsica was also hit by severe weather. Local media reported that a 4x4 vehicle was swept away by floodwaters on Tuesday - one of the occupants escaped through a window, but another man was found dead . Authorities have not released further details about the fourth death.

In the towns of Mouriès and Saint-Martin-de-Crau, between Montpellier and Marseille, dozens of residents were accommodated in emergency shelters after the floods hit. Officials said one person had been injured in that area.

Roads and train lines ‌in ⁠the area were also disrupted, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot wrote in a post ​on X.

"The water has risen to unprecedented levels," Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the Bouches-du-Rhône department, said in a statement on Wednesday.

Witkowski expressed "a thought for all those who are in distress", adding: "We are mobilised at an exceptional level to resolve several issues."

local.title: NY moves ahead on thermal energy test projects
local.summary: The pilot programs in Buffalo and the town of Haverstraw in Rockland County will use utility-owned networks.
local.body:
The state is moving ahead with a series of pilot programs for thermal energy networks, marking a step forward for the renewable energy source in New York.

The pilot programs in Buffalo, run by National Fuel Gas, and the town of Haverstraw in Rockland County, run by Orange & Rockland Utilities, will use utility-owned thermal energy networks or UTENs to provide heating and cooling in neighborhoods and affordable housing developments.

“The number of years it took to get to this point is a testament to the challenge of creating something new … that meets many of the needs of the energy transition we all want to see,” said Rory Christian, chairman of the New York Public Service Commission.

A thermal energy network connects multiple buildings to shared, underground water-filled pipes that utilize the steady ground temperatures to heat or cool indoor spaces.

The PSC selected the two projects from a list of 11 being considered. Department of Public Service staffers looked at a range of criteria, including effects on customer rates and how the proposed UTENs would perform against other methods of heating and cooling.

“Through the extensive analysis conducted, these two pilots demonstrate the most viable projects with the lowest risk,” said Laurie Kokkinides, a policy analyst at the department. “Together they offer broad and distinct learning opportunities.”

Advocates are hoping the pilots are just the beginning. The programs will be evaluated for a couple of years as officials come up with a road map for the use of the technology.

“Then there's more opportunities for us to learn to make the projects more efficient,” said Julie Tighe, president of the New York League of Conservation Voters. “And to be delivering on what New Yorkers need, which is stable energy pricing for heating and cooling.”

local.body: Buffalo school leaders were expected to vote Wednesday on a proposed school closure plan that could reshape the district for the 2027-2028 school year.But after parents, educators and community members voiced concerns during a board meeting, Interim Superintendent Ebony Prophet Bullock announced the vote would not take place that night.WATCH: Buffalo School Board pauses closure plan vote after community pushbackBefore the meeting, protesters gathered to call on the district to slow down the process and give school communities more time to weigh in.Kelly Akamissy, a faculty member at P.S. 90, said staff understand the district is facing challenges but believe decisions about closures should not be rushed."We are here because we understand there's a problem," she said. "We get it. However, we don't make decisions so quickly or abruptly. local.title: Rochester teachers union weighs 'no confidence vote' in Superintendent Rosser
local.summary: Rochester teachers are preparing to hold a no confidence vote on Superintendent Eric Rosser over what the union leader calls a pattern of "reckless mismanagement" in the City School District.
local.body:
Listen • 1:13 Rochester teachers are preparing to hold a no confidence vote on Superintendent Eric Rosser over what the union leader calls a pattern of "reckless mismanagement" in the City School District.

This comes as contract talks between the administration and Rochester Teachers Association have reached an impasse, with a median session scheduled for Tuesday.

"Teachers are clamoring for a vote of no confidence," RTA President Adam Urbanski said. "And I'm saying, 'Okay, give it a little time,' because we want to see if mediation helps. We want to see if (Rosser) joins at the bargaining table in mediation.

"And if he doesn't, then we'll have no recourse but to do something like a vote of no confidence."

Concerns go beyond contract negotiations and a labor agreement that expired in June. Rosser's administration also has not adequately addressed teachers' concerns over student support needs and school safety, Urbanski said. School safety also was at the core of the union’s last no confidence vote back in 2021 involving then-Superintendent Lesli Myers-Small.

When the union surveyed its members in June, hundreds of teachers responded that they do not feel supported by the district and don’t think Central Office understands what is happening in classrooms, according to survey results Urbanski shared.

"If that's not an indictment, I don't know what it would be," Urbanski said. "This district is swimming in money. ... And yet they're skimping on services for English language learners and for special education children."

In a September email exchange between Urbanski and Rosser, obtained by WXXI News, Rosser wrote that there was "significant confusion" regarding the negotiation team's responsiveness to the union, adding that he would continue to "assess progress made to secure a successor agreement."

local.title: New urgent care proposed in Honeoye Falls targets unmet need. Some residents are pushing back
local.summary: The facility to be built on North Main Street would be leased and operated by F.F. Thompson Hospital.
local.body:
Construction is scheduled to start within the next month on a new medical facility in the village of Honeoye Falls that officials said is much needed in that area.

The 10,000-square-foot space will provide family medicine and urgent care services under the operation of Canandaigua’s F.F. Thompson Hospital, part of the UR Medicine network.

“The largest deficit of primary care is in the Honeoye Falls ZIP code,” said Kurt Koczent, chief operating officer of Thompson Health. “The closest urgent care is in Henrietta, and it's about a 20-minute drive. ... This is exactly what a community hospital should be doing.”

This will be the village’s first urgent care center with extended hours, walk-in treatments, and on-site diagnostic services. The address will be 20 North St., which was once a restaurant and has since been abandoned.

Developer Pike Construction is seeking tax breaks and incentives valued at $750,000, or 21% of the estimated $3.6 million project cost — which the company has argued is necessary to offset construction cost inflation. Criticism during an hour-and-a-half-long public hearing last week focused on the veracity of those claims of financial need, and on the tax breaks, specifically a 14-year property tax abatement on the facility.

If the property were transferred to F.F. Thompson, the hospital is a nonprofit and the property would be fully exempt. The facility is expected to employ 26 full-time staffers.

Among those voicing concerns during the public hearing was village resident Cara Briggs.

“This is a very small town and a very small village absorbing the cost of something that is benefitting an area much larger than us, and bringing increased traffic, et cetera, in a town that has one stoplight. And we like that, by the way. One stoplight. Little traffic,” said Briggs, a local attorney who also serves as town justice for the town of Mendon, which encompasses Honeoye Falls.

The Town of Arkwright has approved a
local.body:
ARKWRIGHT -- Back in July, when the Town of Arkwright first discussed the idea of offering a tax exemption to veterans, Supervisor Brian McAvoy called it "the right thing to do." A couple months later, his fellow Board members took action to share that sentiment.

The Town of Arkwright has approved a real property tax exemption for military veterans by local law. Councilman Larry Ball, a U.S. Army veteran, recused himself from the vote, while the rest of the Board approved the local law.

After an inquiry from a resident, McAvoy could not come up with a good reason why not to offer a tax exemption to veterans. McAvoy sought clarity on the potential impact on the town, and after a discussion with Assessor Jeanne Ebersole, McAvoy came to the conclusion that offering a tax exemption to veterans would not be a significant expense for the Town of Arkwright.

McAvoy said it could end up being more of a "ceremonial" gesture than a major benefit to veterans, but that any exemption is worth pursuing. Ball said that as a veteran himself, he feels it is the principle of the decision that matters most.

Municipalities have three levels of exemptions that can be made available to veterans, including disabled veterans, combat veterans, and "Cold War Veterans", applying to all unnamed wars. Each exemption is capped at a certain amount, then equalized.

Depending on a veteran’s classification, they can expect a reduction of $21 to $107 in their Arkwright town taxes, commencing in 2028. The Assessor's Office will be reaching out to the town’s veterans to remind them to apply before March 1, 2027.

Veterans exemptions have been available since 1984, but it took until now for Arkwright to adopt a local law permitting veterans in the town to take advantage. McAvoy lamented that the Town did not adopt the exemptions earlier in his six-year tenure as Supervisor, but was pleased it could be done now.

Instead of shifting the additional tax burden to the remaining residents of the town, McAvoy stated that there is enough money in the reserve accounts to cover the difference. McAvoy wants to use the Town's existing funds and revenue streams, such as the wind turbine revenue, to account for the impact of any veterans tax exemptions.

local.body:
Faez Elias Tayar, age 85, of Portland, NY, passed away on October 17, 2026. He was born on November 25, 1940, in Safita, Syria, and lived a life marked by hard work, generosity, and devotion to his family and community.

Faez came to be known as a man who could do just about anything with his hands and his heart. He took journeyman and trade classes in Syria, building the foundation for a lifetime of skilled work and practical knowledge. He later became self-employed in heating, plumbing, and electric work, operating Tayar Heating Plumbing and Electric in Portland, New York. Through his business, he earned the respect of many for his reliability, his strong work ethic, and his ability to solve problems with skill and determination.

He was a people person in every sense of the word. Faez was outgoing, entertaining, and always ready with a story or a warm welcome. He had a generous spirit and a natural way of making others feel comfortable. He especially enjoyed feeding everyone who came over, and he was known as someone who always took care of others before himself. His home was a place of hospitality, laughter, and good company, and those who knew him will remember the kindness and warmth he shared so freely.

Faez also enjoyed the simple pleasures of life. He liked hunting, fishing, and splitting wood, and he found satisfaction in staying active and useful. These interests reflected the same steady and dependable nature that guided him throughout his life. He took pride in honest work and in the everyday moments that brought people together.

He is survived by his wife, Dawn Babcock; his children, Tara and her husband, Matt Benware, Renee and her husband, Dave Popielarz Jr., and Jeffrey and his wife, Brynn Tayar; and his grandchildren, Courtney Popielarz, Hailey Popielarz, Zachary Popielarz, Chase Popielarz, Galen Benware, Kayden Benware, Hannah Tayar, and Colin Tayar. He is also survived by his brother, Maher and his wife, Suzy Tayar; his sister, Najwa Tayar; and many nieces, nephews, and cousins who will cherish his memory.

He was preceded in death by his parents, Elias and Mediha Tayar, and by his siblings, brothers, Odel and Majed, sisters, Nashere, Najoud, Najat, and Nejla. Their memories remained an important part of his life and family history.

Faez will be remembered for his strong presence, his generous heart, and the care he showed to everyone around him. He lived with purpose, worked with pride, and loved deeply. His family and friends will hold close the many memories of his humor, his hospitality, and the steady example he set throughout his life.

local.body:
ATLANTA (AP) -- Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds to help the Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 on Wednesday night and take a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals.

Rhyne Howard added 16 points and Naz Hillmon had 15 for the Dream, who host Game 4 on Saturday.

It was the second straight strong game for Reese, who had 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, which the Dream also won for their first victory ever in the finals. She now has a double-double in each game of the Finals.

“It feels good when you’re in the finals. It’s a long season and you play against everybody and go through and push through, but when you can do it at the highest level, this is what you live for, this is what the offseason is for,” Reese said. “I put the work in for this moment and I’m just happy I could lead the team to a win. We’re feeling good going into Saturday.”

With the game tied at 49 in the third quarter, Atlanta scored eight straight, including four by Reese. Golden State got within 59-55 on Tiffany Hayes’ layup, but could get no closer as Atlanta closed the quarter scoring 12 of the final 14 points.

Atlanta has dominated the third quarter so far in the series, outscoring Golden State 63-35 combined in the three games.

With Atlanta up 17 in the fourth quarter, Jordin Canada overthrew Reese on the break, but she saved the ball by throwing it over her head underneath the basket to Howard, who got fouled.

Golden State could never recover. Gabby Williams scored 15 points and Hayes added 14 for the Valkyries.

The Jamestown and Chautauqua County Democratic Party committees are asking Charles Nazzaro, a former Chautauqua County legislator who retired in 2021, to replace Vince DeJoy as the county legislator representing District 9 residents in Jamestown.

DeJoy, who submitted his resignation as the District 9 legislator on Thursday, Oct. 15, is moving to North Carolina where he has a new job.

DeJoy's name will remain on the ballot. Nazzaro will serve if DeJoy wins the election.

"We were surprised by Vince DeJoy's announcement," said Marcia Westling Johnson, county Democratic Party chairwoman. "We are excited to have a well-respected public servant and civic-minded person such as Chuck Nazzaro to stand in if DeJoy receives the winning number of votes. It is a short time to voting. We are optimistic that District 9 residents will vote for DeJoy on the ballot knowing that they will be getting Nazzaro as their legislator."

Nazzaro was first elected to the county legislature in 2008 and served for 14 years. He was a Jamestown City Council member before his election to the legislature. Nazzaro chaired the legislature's Audit and Control Committee when either the Democrats or the Republicans controlled the body.

"Chuck is well-regarded by both parties and respected for his budgeting knowledge," said Westling Johnson. "He was the chief financial officer at WCA Hospital for many years. We know he can have an impact on the legislature and county government from the get-go because of his vast knowledge and experience. local.body:
CELORON – Three north county libraries will share a $40,000 state grant to implement the Capable and Connected Caregivers program.

The announcement was made during the Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Library Association's annual meeting held recently. More than 100 librarians, library staff members, board of directors, trustees and supporters of the Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Library Association attended the meeting.

"A $40,000 grant is being shared by the Ahira Hall Memorial Library (Brocton), Dunkirk Public Library, and Darwin R. Barker Library," said Janice Dekoff, association executive director. "CCLS is acting as the financial agent to facilitate the transmission of funds from CRCF to the libraries."

The Capable & Connected Caregiving program meets these caregivers where they already are -- in their local libraries -- and gives them practical training, peer connection, and ready-to-use resources. Piloted across three geographically and demographically distinct Chautauqua County libraries, this program is designed to be replicable, community-owned, and built to last beyond any single grant cycle."

A CCLA report shows that in Chautauqua County, 17% of residents live below the federal poverty line, higher than the New York State average of 13.7%. Additionally, none of the three pilot communities have licensed, center-based infant and toddler slots. Nationally, 32.7% of grandparents living with grandchildren under age 18 serve as their primary caregivers.

"Across Chautauqua County, thousands of children are in the care of people who didn't set out to be caregivers --teens watching siblings after school, grandparents stepping in full-time, and library staff receiving children without the tools to engage them," Dekoff said. "In communities like Brocton, there are zero licensed childcare centers and only two small home daycares, both at or near capacity. Informal caregiving isn't a gap in the system. It is the system.

Dekoff said that the new program aims to deliver training, resources, and peer support through three programs hosted at local libraries:

-Teen caregivers can take part in hands-on workshops at local libraries with first aid, CPR and AED certification; emotional regulation skills, safe snack prep, allergy and medication awareness, as well as resume ready credentials and peer connection.

entertainment.title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Reprises Iconic Role, Yielding Equal Parts Belly Laughs and Boredom
entertainment.summary: The comedian brings back the controversial character for his first big-screen appearance since 2002's 'Ali G Indahouse.'
entertainment.body:
Ali G is older, but not a bit wiser, in his latest big-screen incarnation, the first since 2002’s Ali G Indahouse . And judging by the amount of controversy that’s already been stirred up, Sacha Baron Cohen ’s iconic character of a middle-class white Brit appropriating hip-hop and Jamaican mannerisms still has the ability to rile people.

Marking Cohen’s feature directorial debut, Ali G: Who Iz I? differs from its predecessor with its mockumentary format similar to that of the Borat films . Unfortunately, it’s a decidedly hit-and-miss affair; there are plenty of laughs, to be sure, but many dead spots as well. Being given a limited theatrical release this week, the film will find a bigger audience when it begins streaming on Prime Video. Related Stories THR Cover Story Sacha Baron Cohen Gets Real About Backlash, Death Threats and Resurrecting Ali G Lifestyle Quentin Tarantino's West End Debut 'The Popinjay Cavalier' Sets Launch Date at Phoenix Theatre Ali G: Who Iz I? The Bottom Line A hit-and-miss affair. Release date : Friday, October 23 Cast : Sacha Baron Cohen, Morgana Robinson Director : Sacha Baron Cohen Screenwriters : Sacha Baron Cohen, Anthony Hines, Peter Baynham, Dan Swimer, Dan Mazer, Colton Dunn, Vernon Chatman Rated R, 1 hour 29 minutes

As he did on HBO’s Da Ali G Show (which the character vainly attempts to resurrect now, based on an offer from the cable channel from decades ago), Ali G interacts with real people to greater or lesser comedic effect. From the beginning, the film takes pains to make sure you know that the interactions have not been scripted; after identifying the few fictional characters, including Ali’s very pregnant girlfriend Julie (an admirably fearless Morgana Robinson, taking over the role from the previous film’s Kellie Bright), an onscreen graphic assures us, “Everybody else in the movie is real.” There’s also a brief recap of Ali G to bring viewers up to speed, including clips of past interactions with such figures as Buzz Aldrin and Donald Trump.

There are some scripted scenes involving Ali and Julie, involving such silly plotlines as Ali coming to believe that he’s the biological son of A$AP Rocky (the rapper/actor, along with Rihanna , shows up late in the film to let us know that he’s in on the joke). entertainment.title: Chart Rewind: In 2011, Scotty McCreery’s Debut Album Made Him a ‘Clear’ Country Favorite
entertainment.summary: The American Idol winner was anything but idle as he launched his recording career.
entertainment.body:
When Scotty McCreery won Fox’s American Idol on May 25, 2011 — performing “Live Like You Were Dying” with Tim McGraw on the episode — the season’s end marked the start of McCreery’s country music career.

He didn’t wait to get product into the marketplace. American Idol Season 10: Scotty McCreery , featuring studio versions of 14 songs he performed on Idol , was released immediately, debuting at No. 3 on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums dated June 11. A five-song Highlights EP followed, hitting No. 2 on the July 16 list. Finally, his first album of original songs, Clear as Day , launched at No. 1 on the Oct. 22 chart, days after he turned 18 on Oct. 9.

Produced by Mark Bright (Carrie Underwood, Rascal Flatts), Clear spent six nonconsecutive weeks at the summit and yielded McCreery’s first two top 20 entries on Hot Country Songs, “I Love You This Big” (No. 15) and “The Trouble with Girls” (No. 17).

Over time, McCreery developed greater control of his trademark lower range and began cowriting more of his material, grabbing two more chart-topping albums and, after moving to Triple Tigers, amassing six No. 1s on Country Airplay, most recently with the Hootie & the Blowfish collaboration “Bottle Rockets,” which reigned on Oct. 24, 2025.

Recognizing the 15th anniversary of his recording career, Triple Tigers released McCreery’s compilation 15 on July 17. It includes each of his No. 1 singles and remakes of the former country hits “Hello Darlin’,” “Why Me” and “Your Man,” the latter teaming him with Josh Turner.

Meanwhile, the 2011 Idol runner-up, Lauren Alaina, rules the latest (Oct. 24, 2026-dated) Country Airplay chart with her Chase Matthews team-up, “All My Exes.”

entertainment.title: James Bond Screen Tests to Happen This Weekend: Finalists Emerge for Next 007 Movie
entertainment.summary: The marathon to fit into the tux is nearing its end.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Tomorrow never dies. But for all actors except one, the dream of being the next James Bond will likely die this week.

And that is due to — finally! — a very select group of actors getting in front of cameras to screen test for the role of British agent 007.

According to several sources, Callum Turner , who recently starred in the rom-com One Night Only , and Slow Horses actor Jack Lowden are said to be in the mix for the screen tests, which are taking place in London this weekend. They could begin as early as Friday, according to two sources.

It is unclear who else may be testing. Sources said at least three actors are part of the action but another source says up to five may be putting on the tux to see how it fits. Jack O’Connell ( Sinners ) was rumored to initially be in the mix, but that is apparently not the case, according to sources. And despite some reports, Euphoria and Frankenstein star Jacob Elordi is not testing.

Amazon had no comment and pointed to its previous statement, which said, “The search for the next James Bond is underway. While we don’t plan to comment on specific details during the casting process, we’re excited to share more news with 007 fans as soon as the time is right.”

It is also unclear how involved these tests are, but they are understood to be comprehensive. Sources say there will be three components — stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

Twenty years ago, the tests for Bond included full hair and makeup and a full camera and sound crew on a set. Henry Cavill was among those vying for the role, but Daniel Craig emerged victorious, playing the role from from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die .

Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve is directing the new Bond outing, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing and overseeing the franchise for Amazon MGM Studios, which bought out the creative rights from the Broccoli family in February 2025.

entertainment.title: CMA’s Dolly Parton Tribute: All the Performances, Ranked
entertainment.summary: 'CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Tribute to Dolly Parton' featured performances from Reba McEntire, Brad Paisley and more.
entertainment.body:
When Dolly Parton died on Aug. 25 at age 80, the world mourned the loss of not only a music superstar, but also one of country music’s best global ambassadors, a singular vocal stylist, a vivid songcrafter, a multi-faceted entertainer, a limitless dreamer–and, for many, a moral compass.

On Oct. 21, country music artists gathered at Belmont University in Nashville to honor Parton’s life and career, as part of CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton . As much as the evening’s performances honored Parton’s enduring music, the speeches and heartfelt words from various artists honored the East Tennessee native’s fearless brand of love for humanity.

Reba McEntire welcomed the audience to what she called a “celebration of one of the greatest people I’ve ever been blessed to know.” She also called the evening a “celebration of her heart, kindness, generosity, faith and humor.”

“The greatest thing you can be in this world is exactly who God made you to be…she showed up as Dolly completely, joyfully… unapologetically,” McEntire said, adding, “She became hope, possibility to the little girl growing up with nothing… to the person who felt different and wondered if there was a place in the world for them… she made people believe there was room for them… she made you feel welcome, she made them feel seen.”

“This was a celebration of an undeniable force of nature,” Vince Gill would say of Parton later on in the evening. “Her ability to bring people together from all walks of life is so needed these days.”

A cavalcade of artists, including McEntire, Gill, Ella Langley, Brad Paisley, Carly Pearce, Kristin Chenoweth, Carrie Underwood, Lady A, Darius Rucker, and more joined forces to honor the life, career and philanthropic impact Parton’s career has had. Videos chronicled her career journey, from her early work with Porter Wagoner, to her breakthrough solo hits such as “Here You Come Again” and defining musical works such as “I Will Always Love You” and “Jolene,” to her starring roles in films such as 9 to 5 and Steel Magnolias .

Throughout the evening, the stage overflowed with imagery that paid tribute to Parton, including videos and photos of her work with artists including Kenny Rogers, Porter Wagoner, George Jones, Zac Brown, and many others. The stage was filled with flowers, and lit with Parton’s signature butterfly imagery.

Beyond the evening’s performers and presenters, video tributes poured in from Oprah Winfrey, Julia Roberts, Sabrina Carpenter, Goldie Hawn, and U2’s Bono.

entertainment.title: House Democrats Press StubHub CEO for Answers Over Ticket Resale Fund: ‘Potential Grift’
entertainment.summary: The ranking member of the House Oversight Committee sent a new demand for answers about Eric Baker's firm Andro Capital.
entertainment.body:
Democrats in the U.S. House of Representatives are continuing to probe StubHub CEO Eric Baker about ties between the ticket resale platform and his own broker fund.

House Oversight Committee ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) sent Baker a letter on Thursday (Oct. 22) requesting documents and information about Andro Capital. The letter, first obtained and exclusively reported by Billboard , comes three months after Garcia first opened an investigative inquiry into the fund’s relationship with StubHub.

StubHub disclosed in regulatory filings ahead of its IPO last year that its CEO is also a part-owner and managing partner of Andro, which buys bulk ticket inventory directly from event organizers and then resells them on the secondary market. Baker’s fund has generated revenue of more than $5 million transacting on StubHub since 2022, with StubHub keeping a percentage-based fee of that revenue. An affiliate of Andro, called Colloquy Capital, also has a contract with StubHub to lend short-term financing to other resellers on the platform.

Garcia’s first letter in July was directed to Baker in his capacity as StubHub CEO, seeking records from the publicly traded resale platform to investigate whether it’s engaged in “collusion” with Andro. StubHub denies anything untoward in its relationship with Andro. The company’s lawyers have responded to the Oversight Committee by claiming that Andro is one of several above-board vendors that transparently contribute to StubHub’s overall business.

As conversations remain ongoing between Garcia’s team and StubHub, Thursday’s letter targets Baker instead in his capacity as Andro’s managing partner. This time, the congressman is seeking “information about the role that Andro Capital plays in the ticket market and how the relationship between Andro Capital and StubHub may unfairly raise costs for consumers and limit profits for artists.”

“The financial ties between Andro Capital, its affiliate Colloquy Capital, and StubHub — and your personal connection to all three of these companies — raise concerns that Andro Capital or its affiliates could be receiving favorable placement or other advantages in the resale market at the expense of buyers and sellers of smaller numbers of tickets,” reads the letter.

Specifically, Garcia is asking Baker to provide all communications between Andro and StubHub, as well as an accounting that shows the flow of cash between the two companies. The letter sets a response deadline of Nov. 5.
