entertainment.title: Bernie Taupin Talks His New Solo Album, Working With Elton John and Why He Can’t Name a Taylor Swift Song: ‘I Don’t Listen to the Radio’
entertainment.summary: The legendary songwriter is releasing 'The Sea Has No Mercy,' his first solo album in more than 40 years.
entertainment.body:
Spending two years writing his autobiography, the 2023 bestseller Scattershot , and working on a forthcoming documentary, unleashed a creative wellspring in Bernie Taupin . Explore Bernie Taupin Elton John Taylor Swift See latest videos, charts and news

The result is his first solo album in almost 40 years and the first that Taupin, best known as Elton John ’s writing partner, has ever written solely by himself. The Sea Has No Mercy , produced by Frank Liddell , comes out Friday (Oct. 23) on Vertigo Records/MCA Nashville. Related Queens of the Stone Age Look Road-Ready In 'Tonight Show' Performance: Watch Chappell Roan Brings Out Christina Aguilera at L.A. Concert: 'Honestly Paved the Way for Me' 'The Great And Unmatched': John Anderson Remembered by Blake Shelton, Tim McGraw & More

“The inspiration of the memoir created something in me that started making me write things for myself by myself in the same vein. But at the same time, we started making this documentary, so it was like a trifecta. It was almost this whole idea of different ways of presenting myself without being completely self-involved — which, unfortunately, it probably sounds like,” Taupin says with a laugh.

“I wanted to visualize my past, my present and my possible future very specifically and the only way I could do that was to write these biographical songs,” Taupin, 76, continues, addressing the album’s very personal and reflective nature. “This was a completely 100% selfish endeavor. If other people had assisted me in writing them, they would not have had the cohesive nature that they have.”

The album includes guest vocals from Taupin’s good friend Brandi Carlile , who sings on “Come on California” — a song he originally thought to ask Joni Mitchell to perform on, but Taupin says he told his manager/wife, “I don’t have the balls to call Joni to ask her.”

Taupin will play the Grand Ole Opry for the first time on Nov. 7, backed by The Tennessee Stone Cutters, the musicians who accompany him on The Sea Has No Mercy . His appearance will mark his first public musical performance in nearly 30 years.

Below, Taupin talks about making the album, what John thinks of the set and why he can’t name a Taylor Swift song.

entertainment.title: Billboard & Starlite Announce the Return of Billboard No. 1s to Spain in 2026-2027: ‘We’ve Strengthened This Strategic Alliance’
entertainment.summary: Leila Cobo of Billboard and Sandra García-Sanjuán of Starlite Music Group made the announcement on Tuesday (Oct. 20) during Billboard Latin Music Week.
entertainment.body:
Billboard and Starlite Music Group, the Spanish company that organizes the famous annual festivals in Marbella and Madrid, announced on Tuesday (Oct. 20) that they will collaborate once again on a Billboard No. 1s event in 2026 and 2027, further solidifying the strategic alliance that began last year with the first edition of the Billboard event held outside of the United States.

The announcement was made during Billboard Latin Music Week at the Faena Forum in Miami Beach, Florida, in a panel led by Leila Cobo of Billboard and Sandra García-Sanjuán of Starlite Music Group.

“We’ve strengthened this strategic alliance, and Billboard No. 1s returns to Starlite Madrid this Christmas as part of Starlite Occident, which will take place Dec. 11-23. We will be back for this edition, once again serving as the bridge between America and Spain ,” said García-Sanjuán, co-founder and executive president of Starlite Music Group.

“It’s going to be three consecutive years, which truly solidifies this bridge and this alliance that we are building together — Billboard and Starlite — to create opportunities for artists, so that Latin artists can have their home in Spain and Spanish artists can gain visibility in America through such an important platform as Billboard , which is the Bible of music,” she added.

Meanwhile, Cobo, Billboard ‘s co-executive director of content, said: “This is also part of our commitment to bring the Billboard brand to other markets, and Spain is obviously the gateway to Europe, so we are very excited about this partnership.”

The next edition of Billboard No. 1s Spain will take place in December at IFEMA, Madrid, as part of the programming for Starlite Occident Madrid, a series of concerts that spans two weeks in the Spanish capital. The exact date of the event will be announced soon, and the evening will feature performances from artists who have reached the top 10 of the Billboard Hits of the World Spain Songs chart, along with special recognitions.

The first edition was held in December 2025 and included performances by international Spanish stars such as Ana Mena, Pablo Alborán, Rozalén, India Martínez and Vanesa Martín, alongside legendary Cuban jazz musician Chucho Valdés, American pianist Arthur Hanlon and Lebanese-born violinist Ara Malikian. The event, which drew over 5,000 attendees, marked the first time that Billboard No. 1s was held outside of the U.S., as well as the first time it celebrated music in Spanish.

entertainment.title: Daft Punk Are (Brick) Builders After All in New Collab With Classic Toy Brand
entertainment.summary: The partnership was inspired by a 2020 father-son team's submission to the LEGO Ideas Community mimicking the dance duo's iconic pyramid stage.
entertainment.body:
A home-brewed father-and-son LEGO set paying homage to retired dance music legends Daft Punk ‘s iconic Pyramid stage has helped spark a new partnership between the house of bricks and the “Robot Rock” duo. The LEGO Group announced on Thursday morning (Oct. 22) that its new partnership with the French duo aims to “inspire and remix fandoms” with a pact that promises “product, content and brand experiences” celebrating the creativity and communities of both brands.

The team-up was announced via a short film in which the minifigures representing helmeted French electronic producers Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo follow a holographic red brick through a murky landscape until they reach the “gates of play” that unlock a LEGO brick console. The teaser film is soundtracked by the incessant bass line from “Voyager” (from 2001’s Discovery album) and the title track from the 2005 LP Human After All .

“What makes this partnership so special is the enduring appeal both brands share. Like the LEGO brand, Daft Punk inspires generations through creativity, innovation and a deep connection with fans,” said LEGO Group chief product & marketing officer Julia Goldin in a statement about the partnership. “We’re excited to build on these foundations to reimagine the Daft Punk legacy in a fresh and unexpected way, creating something unique that resonates with fans across all ages. This is just the beginning of a bigger journey – a creative collab made for fans ready to lose themselves to play.“

The new collab was spawned through the LEGO Ideas community, which encourages fans to submit their original concepts for sets that could be turned into official LEGO products. In this case, it was a father and son from Luxembourg whose build won the Grand Prize of the LEGO Ideas Music to Our Ears challenge in 2020, where 10,00 supporters helped boost it to the next level of becoming an official LEGO set.

Their submission, a recreation of the legendary pyramid-shaped stage from the duo’s 2007 Alive tour, began as a family project during the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, according to Patrick Harboun.

“This all started as a creative escape during lockdown between my son and I because of our shared love of Daft Punk and LEGO building,” he said in a statement. “We never dared imagine it would take off in this way. Watching our passion project become part of an official collaboration is an incredible experience, and it’s a reminder of what makes the LEGO Ideas community so special. That a simple idea, shared by fans, really can become something much bigger.”

entertainment.title: Former Virgin Music Comms Head Liz Morentin Launches Strategic Communications Agency
entertainment.summary: Greenvalley Media & Marketing will serve entertainment, media and technology companies and their leaders.
entertainment.body:
Veteran entertainment communications executive Liz Morentin has launched Greenvalley Media & Marketing, a strategic communications agency that will serve entertainment, media and technology companies and their leaders, she announced Thursday (Oct. 22).

Morentin was most recently senior vp and head of global communications and brand strategy at Virgin Music Group. During her run, she led internal and external communications and brand strategy from the company’s launch onward, including subsequent acquisitions and integrations. She supported the company’s global expansion from 12 markets in 2020 as Ingrooves to 36 markets in 2026 as Virgin Music Group.

Prior to that, Morentin served in senior and leadership roles at Warner Bros. Records, Paradigm Talent Agency, Live Nation, RCA Records and Dick Clark Productions.

At Greenville, Morentin will partner with brands and their leaders on communications strategy and execution, including corporate communications, media relations, publicity, executive visibility, reputation management, crisis communications, events and industry marketing. She brings more than 25 years of experience spanning music, live events, TV/film and technology.

“Our industry has transformed so much over the years making it possible for so many more businesses and executives to achieve global success and become highly regarded global industry players, from indie record labels and distributors to tech platforms and media companies,” said Morentin in a statement. “I’m launching Greenvalley to support these businesses and executives looking to build their reputation, grow their business, and reach the right audiences.”

She added, “The agency is named Greenvalley because we believe companies and leaders each have a green space: the distinctive territory where their story, purpose, and opportunity come together. We help clients find that space, build their visibility and reputation, and protect that reputation when it counts.”

“I grew up watching musical guests appear on my favorite TV shows, so having my new single ‘American Reject’ make its debut on Fire Country is a real childhood dream coming full circle,” INK tells Billboard . “There’s something so nostalgic and special about that for me. The song addresses overcoming adversity and using others’ doubts to fuel your passion. “‘American Reject’ is special to me because it’s one that I didn’t have to write. The taping was filled with good vibes, INK says. “What made this experience even more special was how genuinely welcomed I felt,” she says. “Max is a visionary, and he and I hit it off right from jump! The entire cast and crew made me feel right at home. I came in, let my INK spill and they showed me nothing but genuine love.”

entertainment.title: Universal Music Group & AI Gaming Company TYGER Announce Licensing Deal
entertainment.summary: The new agreement allows for UMG songs to be streamed in real-time for gamers.
entertainment.body:
Universal Music Group announced a licensing agreement with TYGER on Thursday (Oct. 22). TYGER utilizes AI to help music adapt in real-time to fan gameplay. The new deal allows for UMG artists to participate, with TYGER users having access to select UMG songs.

TYGER previously had more than 400,000 songs on its platform, primarily with independent artists. The new deal marks their first agreement with a major label.

“Gaming is where the next generation spends its time, discovers culture and connects with friends, but music has never had a native way to reach those audiences,” Nick Venti , CEO and cofounder of TYGER, said in a statement. “This agreement with Universal Music Group is an important milestone for TYGER and validates our vision for the future of music in and around interactive and digital experiences. Together, we’re creating new opportunities for players, developers, artists, songwriters and rights holders alike.”

Michael Nash , chief digital officer and executive vp at UMG, said, “At UMG, we have a well-established track record of exploring and developing new creative and commercial opportunities that enable our artists, songwriters and labels to better connect with music fans. We believe that music has a more integral role in gaming and through this innovative new licensing agreement with TYGER, our artists and their music will now be able to soundtrack personalized gameplay experiences and connect with millions of gamers and fans around the world.”

Earlier this year, UMG also signed a licensing agreement with Spotify for AI remixing on the platform.

UMG CEO Lucian Grainge has been public about his sentiments toward artificial intelligence, telling Nvidia executive Richard Kerris on stage at Nvidia’s GTC AI conference in March that, so long as there are guardrails, the technology may prove useful to the music industry.

“[We are working on] product partners [in AI] that we’re going to be talking about in the next three, five, 10 years, and that’s [going to be] so powerful,” he said at the time. “That’s what’s so exciting, and for me, that’s what’s so inevitable [about AI in music].”

entertainment.title: Ben Silverman Still Doesn’t Want a Job — But He’s Busier Than Ever
entertainment.summary: He walked away from NBC with a stomachache and never looked back. Now his indie shop is juggling Fox’s ‘Best Medicine,’ a Ben Stiller-Benicio Del Toro comedy and a buzzy doc on Sam Bankman-Fried.
entertainment.body:
Ben Silverman has been producing TV since he was 30. Twenty-six years later, the man does not lack for pep. He’s naturally a vibes guy, though the multiple double lattes probably help. On a Monday in late August, Silverman met The Hollywood Reporter at a coffeehouse opposite Manhattan’s Bryant Park to check in on Propagate Content — Silverman’s and his former assistant Howard T. Owens’ production company — but instead golf took over the chat.

The Propagate chairman and co-CEO carries an 8.1 handicap and memberships at the ultra-exclusive Riviera and Hillcrest country clubs. As of late, Silverman’s hobby has informed his profession: Propagate has revived the Skins Game at Amazon, is developing an untitled Anthony Kim documentary and will premiere season two of the scripted Owen Wilson golf comedy Stick on Apple TV on Nov. 4. Meyer Silverman (a plus-2 handicap), Ben’s son and the top high school freshman earlier this month in the Colorado Class 3A Boys Golf State Championships, has already eclipsed Dad’s golf game.

It’s kind of exactly how Ben built on his own parents’ creative careers. His father, Stanley Silverman, is a composer who has arranged music for Sting and Paul Simon; his mother, Mary (Delson) Silverman,was an opera singer, and his stepmother a violinist. “I kind of grew up in the arts but always seeing that it was a tough life,” Silverman recalls. “I had maggots in my cereal growing up. My dad, when he got divorced from my stepmom, had to move in with me and my mom.”

An artist’s upbringing birthed a builder of others’ visions. As the youngest-ever division head at William Morris, Silverman saw the opportunity to repackage overseas formats for U.S. audiences. “That was a quiet business that had a couple of hustling, Willy Loman-type players in it — but otherwise was not a real business,” Silverman says. “I really led the charge in that.”

From London, Silverman adapted Queer as Folk for Showtime and later Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? for ABC. Millionaire handed Silverman his Hollywood “I made it” moment. Massive TV ratings brought in phone calls from Disney chief Michael Eisner — “Thanks! What else you got?” — and NBC CEO Bob Wright: “Why didn’t I get Millionaire ?” (He passed on it but soon would buy The Weakest Link from Silverman.) “I’m like, ‘Oh my God, my life just changed,’ ” Silverman recounts.

With the backing of Barry Diller, a 29-year-old Silverman left the agency to start Reveille Productions, which brought America The Office and Silverman his “I’ve really made it” moment. “My dad and I are sitting together on an airline… and 95 percent of the plane had chosen to watch The Office ,” Silverman says. “The entire plane was laughing.”

entertainment.title: Doc Maker Rocky Mudaliar Signs With Verve (Exclusive)

entertainment.body:
Rocky Mudaliar and his Abrupt Entertainment banner has signed with Verve for representation .

The move follows Mudaliar producing the true crime documentary Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story, a film that chronicles comedian Dane Cook’s rise to fame and the shocking financial betrayal by his own family.

The film about Cook — who at one time was the most successful stand-up anywhere, earning upward of $20 million a tour — debuted earned a Best True Crime Documentary nomination at the Critics’ Choice Documentary Awards on Oct. 13. Brett Harvey directed the Funny Money documentary that will start streaming on Netflix in November.

Vancouver-based Abrupt Entertainment specializes in premium documentaries and talent-driven nonfiction programming.

The signing with Verve for representation will look to help Abrupt expand its U.S. development and production operations. Other doc credits include the Unbreakable: The Dolph Lundgren Story and Inmate #1: The Rise of Danny Trejo , which was released through Universal Pictures.

Mudaliar also co-founded Stage Zero Entertainment alongside music icon Timbaland to bridge traditional entertainment with next-generation music and technology ventures. Mudaliar and his Abrupt banner are currently producing an untitled documentary about a major rock band, with Emmy-nominated and fellow Verve client Sam Lipman-Stern to direct.

As a Canadian company, Abrupt has a track record in international co-productions, production financing and tapping tax incentives and other soft money subsidies to get its documentaries made.

entertainment.title: A Search for His Biological Father Led to a Top Podcast — and an Endorsement From Ira Glass
entertainment.summary: In 'Reaching Out,' Sayre Quevedo has "invented something completely new," according to Glass.
entertainment.body:
As Sayre Quevedo’s latest podcast premiered, he got a ringing endorsement from Ira Glass, who played some of the show on This American Life and said Quevedo had “invented something completely new.”

The podcast, entitled Reaching Out, starts with the premise of Quevedo and his twin brother trying to track down their biological father, whom they had never met and had little information on. This search is interwoven with Quevedo’s diary-like commentary about how he’s feeling about finding his father as well as his own life as he is about to turn 30, and intimate conversations with his brother and mother that delve into how the brothers really feel about each other, and how their paths have diverged.

Quevedo is aided in the process by the fact that he has recorded most conversations in his life since his mid-20s, including across the four-year process of finding his birth father. In the end, these conversations, and his own meditations on identity and family, as well as his noted narrative omissions and motives in telling the story, become the main thrust of the podcast.

“I don’t know if I’ve heard another podcast that tries to capture a person’s life as completely as this one does, and just what it feels like to be alive right now,” Glass said in describing the show.

The six-part series kicked off Sept. 16, from Futuro Studios in partnership with KCRW, and has already won the audio memoir award at the Tribeca Film Festival. The Glass endorsement helped propel the show to the top of Apple Podcast’s series charts that week, with the show still remaining in the top 15.

Quevedo, who has previously created podcasts about his family and partners as well as subjects across the world, spoke with The Hollywood Reporter about finding this innovative format, the state of podcasting and how he feels about sharing his life publicly.

I have been recording myself consistently. I would say since my mid 20s, but I think the habit probably began when I was a teenager. I think it’s almost a habit at this point. I don’t think about recording or not recording, and a lot of that habit stems from the fact that I grew up without really any documentation of my family. My mom left home when she was very young, and my father obviously was not a part of my life, and so I don’t have really any documents of my family history, and so it just became a way of memorializing, of sort of reminding myself that I exist and that I’m a part of the world and part of history.

entertainment.title: Italy’s Movie and TV Spending Drops Amid Tax Incentive Uncertainty
entertainment.summary: The country’s audiovisual sector saw its first inwards investment drop since 2018, the 8th annual APA report revealed at the MIA Market in Rome.
entertainment.body:
Italy’s inward cinema, TV and video-on-demand sectors content investment fell in 2025 for the first time since 2018, the annual APA report released at the MIA Market in Rome indicated.

The overall audiovisual content investment dropped 7.4 percent to €2 billion ($2.24 billion) last year, compared with the 2024 stats, according to the APA, the Italian audiovisual producers association. The dropoff came amid a government overhaul of Italy’s tax credit system for indie producers and local audiences shifting from traditional linear TV broadcasters to emerging streaming platforms.

The latest APA report also comes against the background of an Italian industry dealing with screens of all sizes and new value placed on original IP as storytellers find new platforms to reach audiences. According to the APA report, Italian scripted productions for TV and VOD platforms saw their inward investment fall to €122 million ($137 million), while fiction production dropped to €740 million ($830 million) last year.

“The main factor affecting the sector’s resilience is uncertainty surrounding the public funding framework, from the amount of available resources to eligibility criteria and application timelines. This situation hampers producers’ ability to plan ahead, increases financing costs and reduces margins, placing pressure on all companies, particularly smaller businesses, with consequences for liquidity and investment capacity,” the APA report indicated with commentary.

As elsewhere in the global industry the market share of Italian linear free and pay TV channel continues to fall as streaming platform grew to a 43 percent share in 2025. “In the short to medium term, it is expected to surpass linear television in value,” the APA report warned about the continuing dominance of streaming platforms in Italy.

European producers at the MIA Market this week heard they no longer compete just with each other but against American studios and streamers, YouTube and social platforms. So they require new public and private financing to maintain their audience share and international revenues.

entertainment.title: Yes, ‘Heated Rivalry’ Is Really Headed to Movie Theaters
entertainment.summary: The hit hockey romance series will have special marathon screenings at cinemas around the world including Regal, AMC and Cinemark in the U.S.
entertainment.body:
Have you been hoping to see Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov on the big screen? You’re in luck — Heated Rivalry , the hit Canadian hockey romance series, is officially heading to theaters for limited engagement marathon screenings, distributor Sphere Abacus announced Thursday morning.

The Crave original series, which airs on HBO Max in the U.S., is celebrating its one-year anniversary a little early, with screenings of all six episodes of the first season kicking off on Nov. 6. Sphere Abacus, the Bell Media company that helped bring the show international, partnered with Regal Cinemas in the U.S. for the release. Thursday’s announcement comes after speculation on social media throughout the week. Related Stories Lifestyle 'Heated Rivalry' Goes All In on Physical Media Including Special Edition Blu-Ray and DVD TV 'Yaga' Review: Carrie-Anne Moss and Hudson Williams in AMC+'s Intriguing but Undercooked Brew of Modern Crime and Ancient Folklore

From Nov. 6 through Nov. 30, fans of the show can revisit the series across three paired episode screenings: episodes one and two (“Rookies” and “Olympians”), episodes three and four (“Hunter” and “Rose”) and episodes five and six (“I’ll Believe in Anything” and “The Cottage”). Tickets will run at $9.99 per screening.

Regal will show the episodes in over 275 of its own locations in the U.S. The company also serves as the nationwide distributor, bringing the show to 650 theaters including AMC and Cinemark. Regal showings will include welcome content from the cast and director, show creator Jacob Tierney . Participating locations will offer themed, limited-time cocktails: Summer in Montreal and Russians Don’t Blush.

“ Heated Rivalry is a global phenomenon creating a rush of social media and press activity wherever it lands. We’re very excited to give audiences the opportunity to watch the drama unfold on big screens in North America, the UK, Australia & New Zealand,” Sphere Abacus’ executive director of global distribution and partnerships Hana Palmer said in a release.

Based on Rachel Reid’s novel of the same name, Heated Rivalry focuses on the complicated situationship between Shane Hollander, played by Hudson Williams , and Ilya Rozanov, played by Connor Storrie . The pair are generational talents in the world of professional hockey and sworn on-ice rivals, who meet as teenagers.

The first novel of Reid’s book series, Game Changers , which the novel Heated Rivalry hails from, centered on François Arnaud’s character Scott Hunter and Robbie G.K. ’s character Kip Grady; it served as secondary material for the first season. The show’s season one cast was rounded out by Christina Chang, Dylan Walsh, Sophie Nélisse and Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova.

entertainment.title: Rupert Grint Sets Next Project: Noiser Audiobook Adaptation of ‘Treasure Island’ (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The 'Harry Potter' star will narrate and play every single character in the series.
entertainment.body:
Harry Potter alum Rupert Grint is getting in on the podcast game with a new serialized audiobook of Treasure Island .

In an adaptation for podcast network Noiser, Grint is set to play every single character from Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic 1883 novel, including the wide-eyed Jim Hawkins, silver-tongued Long John Silver, the rum-soaked Billy Bones and half-mad castaway Ben Gunn. Episodes will drop weekly starting Dec. 8.

“Noiser’s serialised audiobooks now reach over 50 million listens a year, which shows how much appetite there is for great storytelling in this format,” Noiser CEO Pascal Hughes told The Hollywood Reporter . “ Treasure Island is where we bring the whole family in. Rupert is beloved by children and adults alike, and his performance is something truly special. Our hope is that kids fall in love with classic storytelling and grown-ups rediscover it.” Related Stories Business Italy's Movie and TV Spending Drops Amid Tax Incentive Uncertainty Movies Stephen Lang, Uli Edel Reunite on 'Mercy Rider' 30 Years After 'Last Exit to Brooklyn' (Exclusive)

Stevenson’s 1883 novel gave the world much of what we now think of as pirate lore — the treasure map marked with an X, the squawking parrot and a deserted island hiding a fortune. When a weathered old sailor arrives at a remote West Country tavern, young Jim Hawkins is swept into the adventure of a lifetime. A treasure map hidden in an old buccaneer’s sea chest takes him from the fog-laden English coast to the sun-scorched shores of a perilous island aboard the Hispaniola. But the crew harbors a dangerous secret, and Long John Silver is not all he seems.

Grint is known around the world for his role as Ron Weasley in the film adaptations of Harry Potter and is set to reprise the role from February to May in Broadway’s Harry Potter and the Cursed Child . He’s starred in Cherrybomb , Into the White , Knock at the Cabin and Servant . His most recent movie role was in the Finnish horror Nightborn , which premiered in Berlin earlier this year , and his next is in Ebenezer with Johnny Depp.

Noiser is a U.K.-based podcast network reaching millions of listeners every week. With hit shows including Real Vikings, Real Dictators, Short History Of and Real Survival Stories , Noiser prides itself on an immersive approach to audio storytelling and high-quality sound design.

Other British stars to have teamed up with Noiser include Dame Julie Andrews, who narrated an adaptation of Emma , and Hugh Bonneville, who narrated some Sherlock Holmes short stories.
